night_defense.Tarawa_learning: US units expect remanned positions and infiltration. Defensive fires are registered before dark; tanks are retained behind likely seams rather than pushed into darkness; illumination is planned but not continuous.
night_defense.finite_capacity: Artillery, destroyer illumination, radio nets and beach roads cannot service every request simultaneously. Local 5-15 minute fire-request/traffic delays occur, but redundant observers and command nets prevent systemic failure.
night_defense.friction: Close-range fighting plus dense artillery/vehicle traffic creates a small non-enemy casualty component; this is included inside sector casualty bands, not added again.

daylight_logistics.beach: Engineer work and pontoon/causeway improvements reduce the worst D-Day exit queues. Heavy equipment can move ashore faster, but debris and road clearance remain rate limits.
daylight_logistics.fire_support: Roi support demand collapses in the morning, allowing some tank/artillery/direct-fire capacity to shift to Namur. Kwajalein retains its own heavy support wallet and does not receive unlimited assets from the northern sector.
daylight_logistics.learning: Suppression reports are treated as temporary until infantry/tanks physically clear the position; broad bombardment increasingly gives way to observed strongpoint reduction.
